chapters.headline: Lillard and Morant: can the Blazers start both, or does Holiday have to start?
Hired and fired in seven hours: the Braiden Bell fiasco and what it says about Dundon's Blazers
Spurs bottom and winless, De Zerbi backed, and City's guilty verdict hanging over everything

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Jack. Are you in a closet? You sound like you're in a closet.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: I'm in the hallway. The apartment echoes now.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: It echoes because you moved the bookshelves again.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Once more. I moved them once more.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: That's three times total, man.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: The light's better on that wall! That's a real reason.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Ha. Has Nora seen the new wall?

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Nora texted me once this week, and it was about the Ducks' depth chart. So now I know the Ducks' depth chart. Probably better than she does.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: That's a dad strategy. I respect it.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: It's the only one I've got. What about you?

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: I gave a guy directions this week. Told him to turn left at the bakery. The bakery closed, like, years ago. He was so polite about it, Jack. He just nodded and walked the other way.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Two years home.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Two years home and I'm still a tourist. The Blazers, though. They're exactly where I left them. Except now they've got two point guards who both want the ball.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Yeah. So who starts? The smart-guy take this week is that Dame and Ja together makes no sense. Both small, neither one a stopper. Start Jrue.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: I'm starting Dame and Ja. And I'm not embarrassed.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Of course you're not.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Hear me out. Dame already said he expects to start with Ja and Deni. Those three are finishing games together no matter what. So the first six minutes are the cheapest minutes of the night. Let 'em learn each other there.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Okay, but here's my question. Cheap for who? Tip-off is when the other team's best scorer is fresh and the game plan's fresh. You're handing him two guys he can see over.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: So you hide Dame on their worst shooter. We've hidden worse. We hid a lot worse for years.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: You can hide one guy. You can't hide two.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Camara takes the best guard, Deni takes the wing, and Clingan's back there eating everything. That's three guys covering for two.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: That's three guys doing extra work every night so two stars can stand at the scorer's table together. In March their legs are gone.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: In March we'll talk.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Ha. Fine. I'd start Jrue, Deni, Camara, Clingan and one of the stars. The other one runs the second unit, where he's the only star out there and he gets the ball back.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Okay, so here's what I've been chewing on. Run your version. Jrue starts with, say, Dame. Who's the bench backcourt?

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Ja and... Scoot.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Ja and Scoot. So Scoot spends his minutes standing in the corner while Ja dribbles. He's 22, he's a point guard, and you've made him a spot-up guy next to the most ball-dominant dude on the roster.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Hm.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Now my version. Dame and Ja start. The bench backcourt is Jrue and Scoot. Scoot gets the ball and runs the show, and he's got a 36-year-old who still guards people right next to him, cleaning up his mistakes. Best classroom in the building.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Huh. I hadn't thought of that. I was so locked on the starting five I never looked at who the kid plays with.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Write that down. I was right about something in September.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: It's going on the fridge. I still think you get torched in the first quarter some nights.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Some nights, sure. We'll lose a couple first quarters in October. I can live with that.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: And who closes?

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Dame, Ja, Deni. And if we need a stop, Jrue for one of the guards.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: So Scoot doesn't close.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Not this year. I know. It hurts to say.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Here's where I'm not moving, though. Ja says he wants more catch-and-shoot threes, and he's talking like he found a new way to play.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: I love that! A guy at 27 looking at his own game and going, there's a room in this house I haven't been in.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Okay. Small confession. I was about thirty, rec league, church gym in Portland. I decided I was going to become a corner shooter. Bought a little shooting sleeve. Stayed after every Tuesday for a whole winter.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: The sleeve. Oh no.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: By March my form was beautiful. I shot exactly as badly as I did in November. Just prettier. Guys started leaving me open on purpose.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Ha! Jack.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: So when a guy who's never shot better than 34 percent in a season decides he's a spot-up guy now, I hear the sleeve.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: You were shooting the same shot! He's saying the shots change. Late-clock pull-ups in Memphis are a whole different job from a spot-up with Dame dragging two guys out to the logo.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Teams are going to leave him open on purpose. Same as me. That's the whole scouting report.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Then he'll make 'em pay.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Bet on it. First week of preseason. If Ja's catching it in the corner and letting it fly like he means it, I mail you the sleeve. I still have it.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: You still HAVE it?

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: It survived three bookshelf moves. And if he's swinging it every time, you buy dinner at the bar.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Deal. I want that sleeve framed. And you know what actually keeps me up at night? Camara. Wide open in the corner, and he swings it to Dame because Dame's Dame. Guys who were here last year might stop taking shots they would've taken.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: That's a veteran thing to worry about.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Camara earned that corner three. If he starts giving it away to be polite, we're in trouble all season.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: So that's Wednesday against Golden State. Ja's corner, Camara's corner.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: And Scoot. I want to see him call a set and get yelled at by Jrue for calling the wrong one.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Speaking of who's yelling during these games.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Ugh. Yeah.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: One day. They hired a play-by-play guy at noon and fired him by dinner.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: With a Fan Fest meet-and-greet on Sunday right in the press release! Come shake his hand!

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: And then they deleted the release.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: A deleted press release. Somebody frame that next to your sleeve.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Start with the easy one. Was firing him right?

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Yeah. And I'm a little sad about it. One of the tweets was basically, I'm not racist, but Asian people piss me off. I'm a Japanese-American guy from here. That's the voice in my living room eighty-something nights a year? I can't.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: He was a teenager, though. Plenty of fans are saying every teenager said dumb stuff.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: They did. I did. He's probably nothing like that kid now. But the job is being the voice of the team. Once it's out, I don't see how he walks onto that floor Sunday.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: I'm with you on the call. What bugs me is the order. A local TV reporter scrolled his feed and found it in an afternoon. So did nobody look, or did somebody look and shrug?

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Lazy's worse. Lazy means nobody in that building cared enough to look.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Mm, no. Shrugging's worse. Lazy you fix with a checklist. If somebody saw that and signed off, you can't fix that person's judgment.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: I think it's lazy. I think it's a building where three people are doing nine jobs.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Which gets us to why the chair was empty.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: They lowballed Calabro. The guy had been calling our games since 2016, and the offer was bad enough that he walked.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: So they dug the hole, preseason's a week out, and that's exactly when somebody skips a step. There's a headline going around this week that basically says Dundon got what he paid for. Brutal. Probably fair.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: And that's where I get mad. The team belongs to the city. You don't go shopping for the voice of the Blazers in the clearance aisle and then act surprised what's in the cart.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Okay, so it's your town, tell me. Do fans actually care about the money part?

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: They care about the voice. Look, my dad. He gave up the season tickets last spring, the stairs got to be too much. So now it's Sunday nights at my parents' place, him in his chair, yelling at the refs half in English, half in Japanese.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: How's he taking all this, honestly?

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: He said, and I quote my father, "So who talks now?" That was the whole review.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Ha.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: But that's it, right? For him the broadcast is the arena now. The guy in that chair is who he watches the game with.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Right, and that's my point. The voice is the money. Your dad lost his guy in July, the day they decided Calabro cost too much. Before anybody found a single tweet.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: My dad doesn't know what Calabro got offered. He doesn't care what anybody got offered.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: He doesn't have to know. He's living with the result.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: See, you make it sound like a line item. He's sitting in his chair on a Sunday asking who talks now. You can't put that in your spreadsheet.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Sure you can. It's the cell that says 'what we saved.' Somebody typed a number in it.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Ugh. I hate that you're right and I still hate how you said it.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: That's fine. I hate that it took your dad's living room for me to say it out loud.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: One more, and I really don't know on this one. The apology goes to the fans and to Rip City. Not a word about the guy.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: What do you think they owe him?

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: I don't know. Something? He's going to google his own name for ten years and this is on top. And it's on top partly because they rushed him into a press release.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: That part's on them. The other finalist was Kevin Draper, right?

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: That's the word. Does he still want it?

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: He wants it. He'll just want more money now. He's the one guy who came out of this week stronger.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Good for him. Check his tweets first, please. Somebody. Anybody.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Okay. Spurs. Tom, I'm saying this one straight to you, because you're the only other person I know who's this miserable. Bottom of the table, five games in. And the CEO comes out encouraged.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: "Encouraged by aspects of the underlying performances."

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: I laughed out loud. And then I stopped, because who am I to talk? I've been saying underlying performances about every Blazers kid since I got home.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Ha. You'd make a great CEO.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Don't say that to me. You've read a hundred of these. Is it real or is it the thing they say right before?

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: I've written one.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Wait, really?

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Big beverage brand, years ago. A guy I'd hired to run a region. Good guy, bad two quarters. I wrote the internal note at eleven at night in a conference room. 'We remain encouraged by the direction of the work.' And down the hall, finance had a spreadsheet open with what it would cost to let him go.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Oh, Jack.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: He read it the next morning and came by my office to thank me. Six weeks later he was gone. He still sends me a Christmas card. Which is worse.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: So the encouraged note buys what, a month?

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: It buys time for somebody to price the alternative. And that one, I'll be honest, I think about more now. Two years ago somebody wrote a version of it about me.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: ...Yeah?

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Yeah. It was a nice note. Anyway. Spurs.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Anyway, Spurs. Okay. So let me be the guy in the conference room. What would actually change my mind on De Zerbi? Old Trafford. The tenth. If we create a bunch and lose, I'll squint and say finishing comes and goes. If we get pushed around, that's shape, and shape's on the coach.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: That's a better answer than the club gave. And here's the thing that might save him. They haven't made a profit since 2019. Paying off a manager is the last thing anybody upstairs wants to do.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: So he's protected because they're broke-ish.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Patience they can't afford to skip. Which is your whole religion, by the way.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Forced patience still counts! And honestly, the international break is my favorite part of the Spurs season now. Nobody loses.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Meanwhile City filed their appeal last night.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Stay with me here. Ten years ago, almost to the day, I was in a bar in Shibuya, four in the morning, tiny TV over the register, the bartender asleep sitting up. Watching that Poch team, Dele, Kane, take on City. I walked home at sunrise thinking, this is the year. And now I'm sitting here wondering if we spent those years chasing a team that wasn't playing by the same rules.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: I'll be the annoying guy for a second. Spurs finished where they finished partly because of Spurs. I'd be careful turning a verdict into a time machine.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: I know. I know.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: So which do you want? Everton just got ordered to pay Burnley, real money. Other clubs smell that. Do you want the money, or do you want somebody to say it?

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Honestly? One sentence. I want somebody at the league to stand at a podium and say, the table you watched in those years was wrong. Those exact words. That's all.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: And then what?

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: And then I'd drive it over to my dad's on a Sunday and read it to him. He doesn't care about Spurs at all. He'd listen to the whole thing, nod, say "took them long enough," and ask what time the Blazers are on.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Ha. That's the most Okada thing I've ever heard.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: That's the dream. That's the whole dream.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: See, I'd take the money.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Of course you'd take the money.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Money buys a center back.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Ha. Okay, fair. And here's the part that really kills me. After all of this, some tiny part of me still wants City to finish above Arsenal.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: There's the Spurs fan.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Bottom of the league and I'm still here, man. Hey, send Nora a picture of the new bookshelf.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: She'll ask about the Ducks.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Then talk about the Ducks. And dig out the sleeve. Warriors on Wednesday.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: It's staying in the drawer. Tom, that's us.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Take care, buddy. See you next week.
